STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This plate looks medium-sized relative to the food, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: no fork or other known object is clearly visible for scale. The cauliflower florets are roughly 3-4 cm across. Across the plate width, the food spans roughly 6-7 florets, consistent with about 24-26 cm.
Final width: about 25 cm (square), so footprint area is about 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:

Thickness is a loose layer, about 1.5 cm average once compressed. Raw leafy greens at 0.15 g/ml: 220 × 1.5 × 0.15 ≈ 50 g. Leaves look fairly wilted and dressed, so call it about 60 g.
- Roasted cauliflower florets (white florets, several visible, roughly 5-6 pieces): footprint about 60 cm², mounded to about 2 cm thick (one floret ~3-4 cm, stacked partly). Average thickness about 1.5 cm. Chopped vegetables at 0.6 g/ml: 60 × 1.5 × 0.6 ≈ 55 g. Round to 60 g.
- Lentil/grain-and-vegetable mixture with dressing (brown-orange mixture in the lower centre and lower left, with red pepper pieces and sauce): footprint about 130 cm², mounded to about 2.5 cm average thickness (a heap of grains about 1 cm per layer, two layers). Cooked grains at 0.8 g/ml: 130 × 2.5 × 0.8 ≈ 260 g. Sauce/dressing contributes some extra mass, so I'll estimate about 260 g for this combined item.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The lentil mixture and cauliflower appear to sit on the plate directly, with no separate base layer beyond the greens. The greens are the base for the right side. No extra hidden layer added beyond what is counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Mixed greens, dressed: about 40 kcal/100 g (dressing adds some fat).
- Roasted cauliflower: about 35 kcal/100 g (with light oil, around 60).
- Cooked lentil/grain mixture with sauce, dressing and vegetables: about 130 kcal/100 g.

Totals: greens 60 g × 0.40 ≈ 24 kcal; cauliflower 60 g × 0.60 ≈ 36 kcal; lentil mixture 260 g × 1.30 ≈ 338 kcal. Total about 400 kcal for roughly 380 g.
